evidence_reviewed: ES query: clearflow-*,clearflow-healthmonitor-* range covering the injection window, sorted by @timestamp
Health witness log: routing-execution: DOWN (consecutive=1) at 21:17:15.326, RECOVERED shortly after
Traced 3 payments submitted immediately after the witness event (b51c883d, 03a2ec5f, 174b3405)
reasoning_trace: Read the witness monitor output first, blind: routing-execution: DOWN, then RECOVERED -- generated by an external poller with zero knowledge of what fault type was injected. Then traced individual payments submitted in the window to corroborate independently. All three payments checked (b51c883d, 03a2ec5f, 174b3405) show the identical pattern: gateway PAYMENT_SUBMITTED, audit AUDIT_CHAIN_APPENDED, validation-enrichment PAYMENT_VALIDATED, aml-compliance AML_SCREENING_COMPLETE, fraud-scoring FRAUD_SCORE_COMPUTED -- every stage up through AML screening and fraud scoring completes normally. None of the three show any routing-execution event at all: no RAIL_SELECTION_START, no RAIL_SELECTED, no LIQUIDITY_RESERVED, no PAYMENT_ROUTED. The pipeline consistently and specifically stalls at the exact stage after aml-compliance/fraud-scoring, which is routing-execution. Two independent signals converge: the external witness names routing-execution directly, and the payment funnel shows the stall boundary exactly matching that service's position in the pipeline. No other service shows any anomaly in this window. Conclusion reached from evidence alone, before reading the injector's own log: routing-execution.
confirmation_basis: Blind conclusion (routing-execution) matches the injector's own ground-truth log exactly. Independently corroborated by two separate evidence sources (external health-check witness + payment-funnel stall pattern), neither requiring foreknowledge of the answer.
